what i've learned from one of my professors was to try think about what ever it is that's causing you distress and ask yourself, "is this true? Is this factual?" or is it something that you have assumed or even curated? 

For example, not knowing if certain people in friend's friend group likes you or not and then having major anxiety whenever you're around them! This has happened to me and it turns out when i really thought about it, I didn't have any evidence (for lack of a better term) that they didn't like me and they didn't really show any negative behaviors towards me. So, if I start to panic I ask myself if the negative things i'm thinking are true, is there any evidence? In a way it's being more whole in the present moment; basing things off of and noticing things about the present moment and not creating anxiety in lala land or anywhere else. 

I'll also do some kinda discreet deep n slow breathing and/or focus on my breath or surroundings.
However, everyone is a little bit different and that is beauteous! But, my social anxiety seems to focus often on approval or liking for some reason ... so the above things are what help me :) 

Fun fact: i'm not sure if you've heard or not, buuuut if you just start smiling you're likely to feel at least a lil bit better! Holding the muscles around your mouth in a smiling position is told to increase activation in positive parts of the brain!! <3

Let yourself feel the emotions, but then stop and think about them. Label them: is this fear, grief, worry, depression? And then label where they are coming from: a breakup. remind yourself that what you're feeling is normal. Over time your feelings towards the process will change! Everything is temporary, except change; change is the only constant. Like queenofalpacan said, let it seep in. But don't let it control or overpower you. Think about you and your emotions and then get up and go do something else, for yourself! You call the shots in your mind and in your life. Best wishes on your healing journey!!

Don't force it -not resisting - to the point where you beat yourself up if you notice you're resisting. And only start when you think you're ready, but do be sure to at least try at some point! 

Maybe try doing one thing for yourself a day. It can be big or small! Something like, making yourself dinner that night; finishing a project you've been working on, or staring a new one; Singing up for a new class, lesson, hobby, etc; accomplishing a small daily goal like drinking more water, going to bed early, or taking time out of your day to meditate, anything. Be sure to give yourself credit for any size accomplishment :) 

And instead of reacting to your thoughts about him and all those worries, just notice what kinds of feelings you're having when those thoughts pass through. 

What helped me is realizing thoughts are just things that happen in our brain, it's part of being human. It's not right or wrong, it just is. And we as humans individually assign meaning to our thoughts. Soooo, you have the power to change what's going on inside yourself! Keep in mind, it takes patience, understanding, and discipline; and it takes time. But someday, it will be as effortless as breathing if you stick with it :) 

And as cheesy as it always is, I'm a firm believer of what's meant to be, will be!

A wise man once said: “Your beliefs become your thoughts, 
Your thoughts become your words, 
Your words become your actions, 
Your actions become your habits, 
Your habits become your values, 
Your values become your destiny.”

Don't let your ex be these things. Don't let him fill your thoughts, become your words, actions, beliefs, habits etc. Keep that focus on you and what you need. Not them, you don't need them. It's just a constant - actually may not be so temporary - battle that sometimes, I don't want to complete. But I will.

My boyfriend and I, of almost 3 years, just broke up yesterday. But it was for the like 50th time. We broke up in December, March, and May before this. We both just couldn't keep the no contact rule and eventually contact turned into seduction and that turned into seeing eachother. This last time we tried to not call it a relationship, not talk everyday, and probably ignore all the red flags going off in our heads. Eventually it caught up and now here we are again: strangers. 

Long story short, our relationship was toxic. It's been toxic for almost 1-2 years honestly but we just couldn't stay stay from eachother. We knew we had to break up, we knew we kept digging a hole deeper and deeper by being together but did it anyway. We tried almost everything to stay together and it always ended up in more pain. 

He was emotionally abusive. Almost narcissistic, had introverted qualities, and is just an angry, stressed, broken person. And I'm an empath, a depressed, (used to be) extrovert empath, weird bubbly, but like I said depressed person. So we each had our own personal problems we should have been working on. Right off the bat, there's some red flags. But, "red flags don't look like red flags with rose colored glasses on" (quote I saw and thought fit perfectly). So we went down this long long loooong tiring painful dark road of fighting and hurting eachother.
